monologue: The card hums warm at fifty, and the weight of three pumpkins rests on the tired wedge. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I press the flat rock down on the slippery wedge, trusting the lean to hold while the memory of stone feels real enough. It feels thin, yet the heavy crops finally settle. I set down a small flat stone beside the box to catch the slip that refuses to move. The air above feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a height I cannot grasp. I wait for the turnip to slide and the card to settle, hoping the wedge does not give in again.

action.why: The wedge feels tired and the pumpkins are heavy, so I must press down again before the slip slides away.

remembered.text: The flat stone felt cool against the hot card, yet it held the weight of the wedge.
The air above feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot grasp.
The wedge feels thin, yet the heavy turnip finally settles.
